newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African farmers arrive in north Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: S.African farmers arrive in north Mozambique.

text.p: The first South African farmers to resettle in Mozambique's remote Niassa province arrived last week, organisers said on Monday.
The initial 14 farmers will settle on a government farm near the provincial capital Lchinga to produce seed for South African farmers due to move to Mozambique in May next year.
The organisers, the South African Chamber for Agricultural Development in Africa (SACADA), said the farmers had been promised the support of Mozambican authorities and the local inhabitants.
"SACADA plans to settle a few hundred farmers during the following three years. Through this, the socio-economic and economic potential of Mozambique can be uplifted," SACADA said in a statement.
The South African farmers' move to Mozambique follows an agreement signed in May by Mozambican President Joachim Chissano and South Africa's President Nelson Mandela.
Under the agreement, land farmed by the South Africans will remain the property of the Mozambican government while control of it will be vested in a joint company, Mosagruis.
The 10-year renewable agreement gives the South African farmers the possibility of settling in areas with few land disputes -- mainly in northern Mozambique.
SACADA said the farmers would initially settle on the state farm because they would not be able to clear permanent land of trees before the start of the rainy season.
"Following this, economic farming units will be measured out for permanent settling of these farmers," SACADA said.

Many South African farmers -- facing reduced government subsidies and higher interest rates -- have expressed interest in the Mozambique resettlement scheme and similar ones in other African countries.
Some farmers, saying they feared that Mandela's government might force them to give up their land to landless black South Africans, have also expressed interest in moving to Angola, Zaire and Zambia.
